text:
Jordan Patel: Heads-up — ACME-X private deployment hitting a networking crash under load. SI says NIC goes into kernel panic during heavy KV cache playback and vendor is flagging a license/packaging requirement for their firmware. Need quick triage from infra + partnerships :phone:.
Samira Khan: How widespread is impact? can we get the panic/logs + customer-visible outage details?
Jordan Patel: Customer sees 3/8 nodes degrade to 100% soft IRQ, requests timeouts. SI collected dmesg snippet, attaching below. They also say vendor asks for signed image + entitlement token before firmware loads.
Alex Chen: paste of dmesg snippet from SI:
```
[ 1234.567890] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000000
[ 1234.567899] CPU: 2 PID: 2048 Comm: ixgbevf/0 Not tainted 5.15.0-rc1
[ 1234.567900] Call Trace:
  ixgbevf_rx_napi+0x1a3/0x2f0
  napi_complete_done+0x5e/0x80
```
Alex Chen: Likely driver/firmware mismatch (ixgbevf vs igb versions). Temporary mitigation: force the host to use the host kernel module parameter to disable offloads or blacklist the vf driver and use passthrough. Example: `modprobe -r ixgbevf && echo 1 > /sys/devices/.../vf_xmit_disable` — risky but can avoid panic until firmware is updated.
Maria Lopez: Partnerships note — vendor (EdgeNet Systems) requires an entitlement file in the image metadata and a signed firmware blob; they won't enable firmware stage unless marketplace contract is attached. I can ping the vendor rep and request an evaluation entitlement for ACME-X.
Jordan Patel: Can Dedicated or hosted fallback be used short-term to avoid outage for ACME-X? They prefer private but will accept brief fallback.
Samira Khan: Yes, we can route critical inference traffic to a hosted model variant for the affected customer tier. Ops: need a routing policy change + canary run.
Alex Chen: Quick safe workaround commands (run on hostctl):
```bash
# temporarily stop the vf driver to avoid panic
sudo modprobe -r ixgbevf || true
# drop heavy prefetch settings
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=262144
# scale down KV prefetch from service: PATCH /service/config { "prefetch": 0 }
```
Alex Chen: These are stopgaps — proper fix is updated firmware signed by vendor / rebuild with their packaging.
Maria Lopez: I'll open vendor escalation and request a signed evaluation blob + license for integration testing. Adding vendor rep to the call now. :eyes:
Samira Khan: I'll open an internal incident for delivery and link SI runbook. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLT-4278 — add ACME-X logs + vendor contacts.
deploy-bot: New incident created by Samira Khan: PLT-4278 — SI integration: ACME-X NIC firmware/entitlement blocker (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLT-4278)
Jordan Patel: Thanks — Samira/Maria/Alex please coordinate on a timeline. I'll notify the customer of temporary fallback path.
Maria Lopez: Vendor rep asked for the tarball + SHA256 and the ACME customer order number. I'll collect and escalate, expect reply within 24h if they prioritize.
Samira Khan: Plan: (1) apply Alex's stopgap tonight, (2) flip routing to hosted canary for critical traffic, (3) vendor escalation for signed blob, (4) validated private image rebuild and staged rollout. Posting runbook snippet in PLT-4278.
Jordan Patel: ACK. If vendor stalls, we'll schedule a meeting with legal + sales to speed marketplace entitlement.
Maria Lopez: On it. I'll update PLT-4278 with vendor contacts and next steps. :calendar:
